# `Q-9-1` — XML Syntax Error

> The XML parser rejected the input as syntactically invalid.

## What this means

Quarto parses XML in a few places — most prominently when
loading a CSL citation style — and uses a strict XML parser
that rejects malformed input rather than guessing. This error
fires when the parser cannot make sense of what it is reading:
a stray `<`, an unterminated entity, an attribute value missing
its closing quote, and so on.

The message names the underlying issue and, where the parser
can pinpoint it, a byte offset into the document.

## Why this happens

Common causes:

- **An unescaped `<`, `&`, or `>` in textual content.** These
  must be written as `&lt;`, `&amp;`, `&gt;`.
- **An attribute value missing a quote** (`name=value` instead
  of `name="value"`).
- **A CDATA or comment block that was never closed.**

## How to fix

Read the byte offset in the message — it usually points within
a few characters of the actual problem. If you cannot spot the
issue by inspection, paste the document into an XML validator
(any browser will do for a quick check) and fix the issues it
reports.

## Related

- `Q-9-2` — unexpected end of input: the parser reached the
  end before finishing what it started.
- `Q-9-3` — mismatched end tag, a more specific syntax failure
  with its own diagnostic.
